body: This looks like it is partially caused by the new_http_archive and bind call in the WORKSPACE file both using the name "zlib". If I change them to be different then it doesn't crash.
Looks like we have the solution here, I'm closing this issue, please reopen if having any more questions.

I have a workaround not a solution, so please reopen (the acls don't let me do it myself.)

The bug here is that bazel crashes on some input, which it should never do, it should instead nicely print an error message if there is an error.

There is also the problem that the workspace file is accepted, and many things work but some particular configuration of rules don't like the reused names. Either using the name twice is an error and there should be always be an error message in that scenario or what ever thing is erroring out needs to figure out how to handle this situation and not produce an error.
https://bazel-review.googlesource.com/c/bazel/+/31892 is the work towards fixing the hard crash. We need to revisit the general question of duplicate names (see also #588, #1952)

### Description of the problem / feature request / question:

I've already solved this issue, it was due to user error on my part.  However, the error message provided by bazel was pretty unhelpful and could use improvement.

The cause of the issue was that I had referenced an external dependency that was defined in the WORKSPACE file.  However, instead of referencing it using the name in the bind statement I referenced it using the actual part of the bind name.  Interestingly if I reference a completely random external dependency name in the BUILD file I see a nice friendly error message instead.  This ugly error message seems to happen when the reference matches some other bit of information in the Bazel build configuration.

For example, WORKSPACE contains:
```
bind(
    name = "ssl",
    actual = "@boringssl//:ssl",
)
```

bind(

)
